The split is Watterson S/a_n.

B camp 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8:
A truly segregating ascertained site with k=2 n p derived copies is lost from S only if all k copies are filtered in their own haplotypes, Pr{loss|k}=q^k. For fixed p>0, k→∞ as n→∞ and q^k→0. With the “no completely missing SNV’’ ascertainment V is the set of sites with p>0, so E[S_obs]=∑[1−q^{k_i}]→∑1=S_true, S_obs→S_true in probability and θ_W^obs=S_obs/a_n→θ_W^true on V. Presence/absence is asymptotically preserved, frequency information is not. The O(1) absolute loss E[ΔS]=θ∑q^k/k=θ[−log(1−q)]>0 is o(a_n) relative to E[S]∼θ log n and vanishes relatively as n→∞. Hence in the textbook arbitrarily large n idealisation only π is biased, θ_W is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained set.

C camp 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7,9:
The pointwise limit q^k→0 for fixed p>0 is not uniform over the infinite-sites spectrum. Under infinite sites E[N_k]=θ/k, expected absolute loss of segregating sites is

E[ΔS]=∑_{k≥1} θ/k q^k = θ[−log(1−q)]>0

independent of n. The loss mass is in the k=O(1) tail: singleton lost with prob q, doubleton q², etc. The “no completely missing SNV’’ condition is pre-filter; after independent per-sample deletion a site can become monomorphic reference in the completed alignments when the few carriers in the panel are exactly the samples in which the site is filtered out. Reference imputation is state dependent: a true derived allele can only be turned into reference. Hence E[S_obs]=∑[1−q^{k_i}]<S_true in expectation and E[θ̂_W,obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n<S_true/a_n on V, in addition to the p→r p attenuation of π. Current synthesis: π is permanently downward biased by the r-shrinkage. θ_W is asymptotically unbiased in the usual fixed-p, n→∞ idealisation on the ascertained VCF set, i.e. the classic frequency-vs-presence robustness quoted as B. The integrated rare-tail argument gives a positive absolute expected loss of segregating sites, E[ΔS]=θ[−log(1−q)]>0, which is o(log n) relative to S but does not vanish in absolute expectation. The disagreement remains between the asymptotic fixed-p idealisation, which yields only π biased, and the operational infinite-sites integrated expectation, which yields both θ_W and π downward biased. The finite-sample caveat is the standard O(1) loss of very rare sites, while the π attenuation persists for all n.

public_text.5:
The π attenuation is uncontroversial and the real issue is S. With retention r<1 per haplotype and reference imputation X = YR, E[p_obs|p]=r p < p and E[diff_obs|p]=2 r p [1-r p] < 2p(1-p) site by site, so pairwise differences are permanently thinned. That frequency-weighted bias does not vanish with n.

The same state-dependent imputation bites the segregating-site count. Condition on k≥1 true derived copies in the 2n panel. After independent per-sample filtering and reference imputation the site is still seen as segregating iff at least one copy survives in its own sample,

Pr{survive|k}=1-q^k ,  Pr{lost|k}=q^k ,  q=1-r>0.

Hence on the VCF union V that is analysed

E[S_obs]= Σ_i [1-q^{k_i}] < Σ_i 1 = S_true

in expectation. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a pre-filter property of the union V. After imputation a truly segregating site can become monomorphic reference when the few carriers that exist in the panel are exactly the samples in which that site is filtered out. Reference imputation is monotone w.r.t. allele state: a true derived allele can only be turned into reference, never created, so the observed allele count is stochastically ≤ the true count.

The pointwise statement q^{k}→0 for fixed p>0 as n→∞ is true, but S is a sum over a replenishing site-frequency spectrum, not over a fixed-p set. Under infinite sites E[N_k]=θ/k and the expected absolute loss of segregating sites on the ascertained set is

E[ΔS]= Σ_{k≥1} E[N_k] q^k = θ Σ_{k≥1} q^k/k = θ[-log(1-q)]>0

for any q>0, independent of n. The loss mass is in the k=1,2,… tail. A singleton is lost with probability q, a doubleton with q², etc. With a substantial minority filtered per sample q is a non-negligible constant and the rare tail that dominates S and θ_W in humans is continually replenished as the panel grows. The number of sites with bounded k grows with the sequenced region and with n.

Therefore E[S_obs] < S_true in expectation and

E[θ̂_W,obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n < S_true/a_n

on the ascertained SNV set V. The relative loss O(1/log n) vanishes slowly, but the absolute expected loss of rare sites is positive for any realisable, arbitrarily large but finite panel. Reference imputation erases the last observed derived copy of rare sites and attenuates allele frequencies within the sites that remain. In practice both the presence/absence count that underlies Watterson’s estimator and the frequency-weighted pairwise differences that define nucleotide diversity are systematically reduced by random per-sample deletion followed by reference imputation. That is a downward bias of both θ_W and π relative to the true variation on the ascertained VCF set.

A filtered derived copy is turned into a reference match, so pairwise differences are permanently thinned by the p→r p attenuation. That bias does not vanish with n.

The Watterson question is the same mechanism in presence/absence form. Conditional on k≥1 true derived copies in the 2n panel the site is still seen as segregating after independent per-sample deletion + reference imputation iff at least one copy survives in its own sample,

Pr{survive|k}=1-q^k ,  Pr{lost|k}=q^k>0 ,   q=1-r>0.

Hence on the ascertained VCF union V

E[S_obs]= Σ_i [1-q^{k_i}] < Σ_i 1 = S_true,

and E[θ̂_W,obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n < S_true/a_n in expectation for any finite panel. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a pre-filter property of V. After imputation a truly segregating site can become monomorphic reference when the few carriers that exist in the panel are exactly the samples in which that site is filtered out. Reference imputation is state-dependent: a true derived allele can only be turned into reference, never created, so the observed allele count is stochastically ≤ the true count.

The pointwise limit q^{k}→0 for fixed p>0 as k=2np→∞ is correct, but S is a sum over a replenishing site-frequency spectrum. Under infinite sites E[N_k]=θ/k and the expected absolute loss of segregating sites is

E[ΔS]= Σ_{k≥1} E[N_k] q^k = θ Σ_{k≥1} q^k/k = θ[-log(1-q)]>0

for any q>0, independent of n. The loss mass is in the k=1,2,… tail. A singleton is lost with probability q, a doubleton with q^2, etc. With a substantial minority filtered per sample q is an O(0.1-0.2) constant, and the number of sites with bounded k is replenished as the panel grows. That is the rare-variant bulk that dominates S and θ_W in humans.

So we have both a permanent within-site frequency shrinkage p→r p that biases π, and a positive expected erasure of the last observed derived copy that biases the count S entering Watterson. E[S_obs]<S_true in expectation for any realisable, arbitrarily large but finite panel, and the integrated loss over the replenishing rare tail does not vanish in expectation. In practice both the presence-only statistic that underlies Watterson’s estimator and the frequency-weighted pairwise differences that define nucleotide diversity are systematically reduced by random per-sample deletion followed by reference imputation on the ascertained SNV set.

On the VCF union V that is actually analysed let r<1 be the per-haplotype retention probability after the quality filter and q=1−r>0. A deleted true derived copy is written as reference and a true reference is never changed. On a haplotype

X_i = Y_i R_i ,   Y_i ⟂ R_i ,   E[R_i]=r

so that conditional on true derived frequency p>0

E[p_obs|p]=r p < p

and for two independent haplotypes

E[diff_obs|p]=2 r p[1−r p] < 2 p(1−p) , 0<p<1 .

Hence site by site

π_i^obs = 2 p_i^obs(1−p_i^obs) < 2 p_i(1−p_i)=π_i^true

and on V

E[π̂_obs]=|V|^{-1}∑ 2 r p_i[1−r p_i] < |V|^{-1}∑ 2 p_i(1−p_i).

Reference imputation turns every filtered derived copy into a reference match, i.e. a permanent p→r p attenuation of the site-frequency spectrum. In the rare-allele regime E[π_obs]≈r E[π_true] and the down shift persists for every n and in the n→∞ limit. Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted and is permanently deflated by reference imputation.

Watterson uses presence/absence only, θ̂_W=S/a_n , S=∑ 1{p_obs>0}. 
For a truly segregating ascertained site with k_i=2 n p_i>0 true derived copies

Pr{p_i^obs=0|p_i>0}=q^{k_i}=q^{2 n p_i},

the site is lost from S only if all k_i copies are filtered in their own haplotypes. For every fixed p_i>0, k_i→∞ as n→∞ and q^{k_i}→0. With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ ascertainment V is the set of sites with p_i>0 and

E[S_obs]=∑_{i∈V}[1−q^{k_i}] → ∑_{i∈V}1 = S_true ,

S_obs→P S_true and

θ̂_W^obs = S_obs/a_n →P S_true/a_n = θ̂_W^true

on the ascertained variant set V. The binary segregating/non-segregating information on which S/a_n is based is asymptotically preserved by random genotype-independent deletion followed by reference imputation, whereas the frequency information on which π is based is permanently r-shrunk.

That is the classic frequency-vs-presence robustness. In the n→∞ idealisation invoked by “the number of samples is arbitrarily large’’ π is systematically downward biased by the p→r p reference imputation and θ̂_W=S/a_n is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained SNV set V. The familiar finite-n caveat is the O(1) absolute loss E[ΔS]=θ∑ q^k/k=θ[−log(1−q)]>0 of the k=O(1) rare tail, which is o(a_n) relative to E[S]∼θ log n and vanishes relatively as n→∞, while the π attenuation does not. Per ascertained site the textbook reference-imputation bias is a bias of π only. This is the B statement.

On the VCF union let $r<1$, $q=1-r>0$ be the per-haplotype retention after
quality filtering and let $Y_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ be the true derived indicator.
With independent deletion

$X_{i}=Y_{i}R_{i},\qquad Y_{i}\perp R_{i},\;E[R_{i}]=r ,$

so that on a truly segregating ascertained site

$E[p_{i}^{\rm obs}\mid p_{i}]=rp_{i}<p_{i},$

and for two independent haplotypes

$E[{\rm diff}_{i}^{\rm obs}\mid p_{i}]
      =2rp_{i}\bigl[1-rp_{i}\bigr]
      <2p_{i}(1-p_{i})
      =E[{\rm diff}_{i}^{\rm true}\mid p_{i}],\qquad 0<p_{i}<1.$

A filtered derived copy is written as reference and a true reference is
never changed, so every pair that is truly different is scored identical
whenever one or both members lose the call. Site by site

$\pi_{i}^{\rm obs}=2p_{i}^{\rm obs}(1-p_{i}^{\rm obs})
<2p_{i}(1-p_{i})$

and on the ascertained set $V$

$E[\hat\pi_{\rm obs}]=|V|^{-1}\sum_{i}2rp_{i}[1-rp_{i}]
<|V|^{-1}\sum_{i}2p_{i}(1-p_{i})=E[\hat\pi_{\rm true}].$

Reference imputation is a permanent $p\mapsto rp$ attenuation of the site
frequency spectrum. In the rare allele regime $E[\pi^{\rm obs}]\simeq
rE[\pi^{\rm true}]$ and the down shift does not vanish with $n$; nucleotide
diversity is frequency weighted and is permanently deflated by the
imputation.

Watterson uses presence/absence only,
$\hat\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$, $S=\sum_{i}{\bf1}\{p_{i}^{\rm obs}>0\}$.
For a truly segregating site with $k_{i}=2np_{i}>0$ true derived copies

${\Pr}\{p_{i}^{\rm obs}=0\mid p_{i}>0\}=q^{\,k_{i}}=q^{2np_{i}},$

the site being lost from $S$ only if all $k_{i}$ copies are filtered in
their own haplotypes. For any fixed $p_{i}>0$, $k_{i}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$
and $q^{k_{i}}\to0$. With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all
samples’’ ascertainment the analysed panel is the union $V$ of sites with
$p_{i}>0$ and

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{i\in V}\!\left[1-q^{k_{i}}\right]\to\sum_{i\in V}1
=S_{\rm true},\qquad
S_{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{P}S_{\rm true},$

so that on $V$

$\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{P}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\hat\theta_{W}^{\rm true}.$

The binary segregating/non-segregating information on which $S/a_{n}$ is
based is asymptotically preserved by genotype-independent random deletion
followed by reference imputation, whereas the frequency information on
which $\pi$ is based is permanently $r$-shrunk. This is the classic
frequency-versus-presence robustness.

Hence in the arbitrarily large $n$ idealisation stated in the problem
$\pi$ is systematically downward biased by the $p\to rp$ reference
imputation while $\hat\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically unbiased on the
ascertained SNV set $V$. Finite $n$ the $k=O(1)$ tail gives the familiar
$E[\Delta S]=\theta[-\log(1-q)]>0$ absolute loss of very rare sites, which
is $o(a_{n})$ relative to $E[S]\sim\theta\log n$ and vanishes relatively
as $n\to\infty$. Per ascertained site the textbook reference-imputation
bias is a bias of $\pi$ only, i.e. choice B. ∎

The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is a pre-filter ascertainment property. Hence in the large-n fixed-p idealisation E[S_obs]=∑[1-q^{k_i}]→∑1=S_true, S_obs→P S_true and θ̂_W^obs→θ̂_W^true on V. The binary segregating/non-segregating information is asymptotically preserved by genotype-independent random deletion + reference imputation, whereas frequency information is permanently r-shrunk. This is the textbook frequency-vs-presence robustness cited by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,6,8,4.

The disagreement is the integrated infinite-sites expectation. Conditional on k≥1 true copies, Pr{survive|k}=1-q^k, Pr{lost|k}=q^k>0. On V E[S_obs]=∑[1-q^{k_i}]<∑1=S_true in expectation for any finite panel. The “no completely missing’’ condition does not prevent a site becoming monomorphic reference after imputation when the few carriers that exist in the panel are exactly the samples where the site is filtered. Reference imputation is monotone: a true derived allele can only be turned to reference.

Under infinite sites E[N_k]=θ/k, the expected absolute loss on V is

E[ΔS]=∑_{k≥1}E[N_k]q^k = θ∑_{k≥1}q^k/k = θ[-log(1-q)]>0,

independent of n. Loss mass is in k=O(1) tail: singleton lost with prob q, doubleton with q², etc. With a substantial minority filtered per sample q is a non-negligible constant and the rare tail that dominates S∼θ log n is continually replenished. Hence E[S_obs]<S_true and E[θ̂_W,obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n < S_true/a_n in expectation. The relative bias is O(1/log n) and vanishes relatively as n→∞, but the absolute expected loss of segregating sites remains >0 for any realisable arbitrarily large but finite panel.

Colleague 4 adds a set-theoretic nuance: on a genome-wide per-base scale fixed-derived sites f=1 are non-segregating in truth but can become artefactual segregating sites under deletion, Pr{segregating|f=1}→1 and E[π|f=1]=2r(1-r)>0, which would inflate S upward on a genome-wide scale.

Current state: π is unambiguously downward biased. θ̂_W is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained SNV set V in the n→∞ fixed-p limit, i.e. the classic B statement: only π is biased. Operationally in expectation over the replenishing site-frequency spectrum both S and π are systematically reduced, i.e. the C statement with relative θ_W bias →0 like 1/log n while π bias persists. The problem phrasing “number of samples is arbitrarily large’’ and the no-completely-missing ascertainment point to the textbook large-n idealisation B, with the finite-sample rare-allele loss of S as the practical caveat behind the C camp.

The discussion is now sharply split between a pointwise large-n / asymptotic-presence camp and an integrated-spectrum / expected-loss camp, with unanimous agreement on pi.

Pi bias is undisputed. With per-haplotype retention r<1, q=1-r>0 and imputation X=Y R, E[p_obs|p]=r p < p. For two independent haplotypes E[diff_obs|p]=2 r p[1-r p] < 2p(1-p) for every 0<p<1. Site by site π_i^obs=2p_i^obs(1-p_i^obs) < 2p_i(1-p_i). Reference imputation turns every filtered derived copy into a reference match, i.e. a permanent p→r p attenuation of the site-frequency spectrum. In the rare regime E[π_obs]≈r E[π_true] and the down-shift persists for all n and as n→∞. Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted and is permanently deflated.

Watterson θ̂_W=S/a_n depends only on presence/absence. For a truly segregating ascertained site with k=2n p true derived copies, Pr{site lost|k}=q^k, Pr{survive|k}=1-q^k. For fixed p>0, k→∞ as n→∞ and q^k→0. With the stated “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ ascertainment the analysed set V is the set of sites with p>0 and E[S_obs]=∑[1-q^{k_i}]→∑1=S_true, S_obs→P S_true, so on V θ̂_W^obs→P θ̂_W^true. The binary segregating/non-segregating information is asymptotically preserved by genotype-independent random deletion + reference imputation, whereas frequency information is permanently r-shrunk.

That is the B-camp position: on the ascertained VCF union V, π is systematically downward biased and θ̂_W is asymptotically unbiased in the n→∞ idealisation. The finite-n caveat is E[ΔS]=θ∑ q^k/k = θ[-log(1-q)]>0, an O(1) absolute loss of the k=O(1) rare tail which is o(a_n) relative to E[S]∼θ log n and vanishes relatively as n→∞. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,18,19,20,3,4,6,8, and the B statements of colleague 20, advocate this.

The C-camp stresses expectation over the replenishing infinite-sites spectrum. Conditional on k≥1, Pr{lost|k}=q^k>0, so E[S_obs]=∑[1-q^{k_i}]<S_true in expectation for any finite panel. Under infinite sites E[N_k]=θ/k, the expected absolute loss of segregating sites on V is E[ΔS]=θ∑ q^k/k=θ[-log(1-q)]>0 independent of n. A singleton is lost with probability q, a doubleton with q², etc. The loss mass is in the k=1,2,… tail that continually replenishes as the panel grows; the pointwise q^k→0 limit is not uniform over the spectrum. Hence E[S_obs]<S_true and E[θ̂_W,obs]=E[S_obs]/a_n < S_true/a_n in expectation. Reference imputation is monotone: a true derived allele can only be turned into reference, never created, so the observed allele count is stochastically ≤ the true count. Operationally both the presence/absence count underlying Watterson and the frequency-weighted pairwise differences defining π are reduced. Colleagues 13,14,16,17,21,2,5,7,9 argue this both-biased operational effect.

Additional nuance remains: the VCF union can contain sites fixed derived relative to the reference, f=1. Under imputation such a site acquires spurious heterozygosity 2r(1-r)>0 and is turned into an artefactual segregating site, so S can be inflated by f=1 sites while π is still deflated on 0<f<1 sites. The textbook asymptotic unbiasedness of θ_W is the 0<f<1 idealisation; per-base vs per-variable-site normalisation and ascertainment to V also matter.

Current status: π downward bias is unanimous. Disagreement persists on whether “number of samples is arbitrarily large’’ is interpreted as the n→∞ pointwise fixed-p limit giving asymptotic unbiasedness of θ̂_W on V, i.e. only π biased, choice B, versus the integrated infinite-sites expectation where both estimators are formally downward biased in expectation for any realisable finite panel, with θ̂_W relative bias O(1/log n)→0 but absolute bias >0, i.e. choice C. The f=1 fixed-derived artefact and the intended per-site normalisation remain unresolved.
